- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is trending up, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is trending down, avoid excessive downward correction — allow slight lagged rebound.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model should not overcorrect downward; maintain slight upward bias.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from forecast in first 5 days, adjust future days downward if sentiment remains neutral or negative.  
- If sentiment history shows rising volatility (e.g., alternating +0.3 to -0.2), model should smooth out sharp forecast swings to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.  
- When sentiment is high but price is stuck near support, forecast should not assume continuation — expect mean reversion toward prior 10-day average.
